links.outcome: Structured expert rubric evaluation versus BLEU/ROUGE/BERTScore in classifying clinically appropriate LLM responses
links.effect: Quantitative metrics frequently misclassified clinically appropriate responses as inaccurate; S.C.O.R.E. showed Cronbach's α 0.745 in the optimized domain and Cliff's δ 0.68-0.92 for optimization status.
links.quote: While quantitative metrics frequently misclassified clinically appropriate responses as inaccurate, S.C.O.R.E. demonstrated acceptable internal consistency (Cronbach's α 0.745) in the hyperparameter-optimized domain and detected large effect sizes (Cliff's δ 0.68-0.92) reflecting optimization status.

unlisted_practices: Domain-specific hyperparameter tuning of LLMs, with detection through expert evaluation
Five-dimensional structured expert evaluation framework (S.C.O.R.E.) for open-ended LLM responses

screen.reason: The study develops and empirically evaluates a structured multidimensional framework (S.C.O.R.E.) for clinical validation and safety assessment of open-ended LLM outputs against standard automated metrics across multiple medical specialties.

primary.practice: structured expert evaluation framework for safety and validation
